title: The Wright brothers' homemade wind tunnel
dek: Their glider didn't lift the way the published numbers said it would. So they built a way to measure it themselves.
paragraphs: In 1901, Wilbur and Orville Wright tested a glider that produced far less lift than they had calculated from the figures of the day.

Rather than guess, they decided to measure. In late 1901, in Dayton, Ohio, they built a small wind tunnel: a long wooden box with a fan driving air through it, plus balances to measure the forces on small model wings.
They tested many model wing shapes at many angles, writing down every result.
Their data led to a much better glider in 1902, and in December 1903 their powered Flyer made the first flights.
takeaway: When a project doesn't behave the way the instructions say, test small and change one thing at a time. A careful notebook beats a lucky guess.
